key_facts: § 8-1-190(b)(4): an agent, servant or employee may agree with a commercial entity to refrain from carrying on a like business in a specified area; restraints of two years or less are presumed reasonable.
§ 8-1-190(b)(5): an employee may agree not to solicit current customers; restraints of 18 months, or as long as post-separation consideration is paid, whichever is greater, are presumed reasonable.
§ 8-1-190(b)(3): a seller of business goodwill may agree not to compete; one year or less is presumed reasonable.

§ 8-1-191(a): protectable interests are trade secrets, confidential information, commercial relationships with specific customers, goodwill, and specialized training involving substantial expenditure set out in writing as consideration; § 8-1-191(b): job skills alone are not protectable.

Job skills in and of themselves, without more, are not protectable interests. (§ 8-1-191(b))
The party seeking enforcement of the covenant has the burden of proof on every element. (§ 8-1-194)
Nothing in this article shall be construed to eliminate any professional exemption recognized by Alabama law. (§ 8-1-196)

population: Federal security-clearance process (all agencies; DCSA/NBIS)
effect: Fastest 90% of initial Top Secret clearances averaged 206 days against a 114-day goal, FY2025 Q2
summary: GAO's 2026 review of NBIS development and clearance timeliness. It reports that agencies missed timeliness goals for nearly all phases, gives the Top Secret initial-clearance average for FY2025 Q2, and reports continuous-vetting alert volumes. Two related GAO items (GAO-25-108721, September 2025; the 2025 High-Risk List GAO-25-107743) are folded into its key facts.
key_facts: As of FY2025 Q2, the fastest 90% of initial Top Secret clearances averaged 206 days against a 114-day goal (92 days over).
Continuous-vetting alerts requiring review rose from about 30,000 per quarter in FY2023 to over 100,000 in FY2025 Q3.
DoD projects about \$2.2 billion more NBIS development spending through FY2031, after \$2.4 billion spent through FY2024 on NBIS and legacy systems.
One-third of agencies surveyed in May 2025 said NBIS delays disrupted continuous-vetting implementation.
GAO-25-108721 (2025-09-16): major NBIS development complete by end of FY2027; original full-operation target was 2019.
GAO 2025 High-Risk List (GAO-25-107743, 2025-02-25): 'Government-wide Personnel Security Clearance Process' remains one of 38 areas, meeting 2 of 5 criteria and partially meeting 3.
quotes: federal agencies have not met timeliness goals for nearly all phases of the security clearance process (Highlights)
